class_def.title: Class definition
class_def.description: Dotted module path and class name of a Python class, as 'module:ClassName' or 'package.module:ClassName'. Module parts are lower snake_case; the class name is CapWords and may carry consecutive capitals.

template_var.title: Template Variable
template_var.description: A template variable reference, substituted at instantiation time. Must start with '$' followed by letters, digits, or underscores.
template_var.markdownDescription: A template variable reference, substituted at instantiation time. Must start with `$` followed by letters, digits, or underscores.

blackboard_pointer.title: Pointer to Command Generator Blackboard Value
blackboard_pointer.description: Pointer to Command Generator Blackboard Value

entity_id.title: Entity ID
entity_id.description: Either number or name uniquelly specifying the entity.

entity_id_int.title: Entity ID number
entity_id_int.description: Unique number assigned by the game automatically to any entity in the game.

entity_id_str.title: Entity ID name
entity_id_str.description: Unique name assigned by the designer to any entity in the game.

entity_ttl.title: TTL before deletion
entity_ttl.description: How many miliseconds should the entity persist before deletion.

entity_action.title: Entity Actions
entity_action.description: Possible game actions for the entity

entity_direction.title: Entity Direction
entity_direction.description: Possible move directions for the entity.

entity_weapon_type.title: Entity Weapon Type
entity_weapon_type.description: Possible weapon types for the entity.

entity_damage.title: Entity Damage
entity_damage.description: Damage. May also be a template variable, since entity and template definitions are parameterised before instantiation.

entity_template_path.title: Entity Template Path
entity_template_path.description: Path or id of an entity definition used as a template, relative to ENTITY_PATH and without the file extension. May carry parameters in brackets.

template_ref.title: Template Reference
template_ref.description: A template to apply. Either a name string, optionally with parameters in brackets, or a list of [name], [name, [args]], [name, {kwargs}] or [name, [args], {kwargs}] - the four list forms pgrpg.functions.str_utils.parse_fnc_list accepts.

allOf.description: With all three items present the second is positional args and must be a list; a lone second item may be either args or kwargs.
